 # Analysis Trace
 
 ## Objective
 
-Assess whether plasma protein changes after feminizing GAHT are consistent with menopause or menopausal hormone therapy (MHT). Menopause is reported separately as a sensitivity/comparator analysis, not pooled with MHT.

-Yes. A WGCNA-style unsigned co-expression analysis identified coordinated ALS-associated modules in bulk spinal-cord RNA-seq.
+Yes, WGCNA can identify co-expressed modules, but the corrected ALS-only signed analysis provides conservative evidence here. Cervical retained one 228-gene module; its ALS-control eigengene difference was +0.228 (Welch t=1.24, p=0.22). Lumbar and thoracic also retained broad modules without significant disease associations.
 
-The strongest cervical module (88 genes) was increased in ALS (eigengene delta +1.17, Welch t=7.26, p=1.19e-9, FDR=1.07e-8) and contained APOE, AIF1, CD68, CD74, MS4A7 and CD53, consistent with an immune/myeloid activation program. Other cervical modules were reduced and included neuronal/oligodendrocyte-associated genes such as CNP and OPALIN, plus a mitochondrial-enriched module. Lumbar cord independently showed the same pattern: an immune module (76 genes; delta +0.83, p=1.7e-6, FDR=6.9e-6) and two reduced modules (83 genes, delta −0.875, p=2.7e-7; 125 genes, delta −0.66, p=2.0e-5).
+Using the fixed cervical membership, overlap was 227/228 genes in cervical, 146/228 in lumbar, and 125/228 in thoracic. Transfer associations were nonsignificant (lumbar delta +0.036, p=0.80; thoracic delta +0.266, p=0.39), so independent replication should not be claimed.
 
-Thoracic modules were directionally suggestive but did not pass FDR 0.05 (n=52). These findings support coordinated glial/immune activation and loss of neuronal/oligodendrocyte-associated expression programs, but bulk RNA cannot distinguish regulation within cells from changed cell composition. No supplied proteomics table was available for orthogonal validation, and causality cannot be inferred.
+Formal Mathys marker enrichment was completed with one-sided Fisher tests for astrocyte, microglia, oligodendrocyte, and excitatory-plus-inhibitory neuron markers, using all analyzed genes as the universe and BH correction. Complete results and contingency tables are in module_marker_enrichment.tsv; module memberships and eigengenes are also saved as TSV files.
+
+The result supports feasibility of co-expression analysis, not a definitive ALS dysregulation signature. Bulk composition, small thoracic n, gene filtering/tree-cut choices, and absent proteomics limit interpretation.

 # Objective
 
-The question is whether weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) can identify coordinated gene programs dysregulated in ALS spinal cord. Success was defined as finding reproducible, sufficiently large co-expression modules whose sample eigengenes differ between ALS and controls, with biologically coherent hub genes and concordance across spinal levels. This is an association analysis, not proof that ALS causes the program.
+Test whether co-expressed ALS spinal-cord gene programs can be identified by a defensible WGCNA workflow. Success means modules are discovered using ALS samples only, have inspectable memberships/eigengenes, and their ALS/control associations and cell-marker enrichments are quantified. Cross-level claims require fixed membership transfer, not separately discovered module labels.
 
 # Data Sources
 
-All paths below are relative to `./data`.
-
-- `Cervical_Spinal_Cord_gene_counts.tsv.gz`: 58,884 genes x 176 columns (2 annotation columns plus 174 samples); integer raw counts. The first fields are `ensembl_id`, `gene_name`; samples include `sample_124`.

Lumbar: 154 x 43; `ALS` 119, `Control` 33, `ALS-FTD` 1, `ALS-AD` 1. Thoracic: 52 x 43; ALS 41 and Control 11. Key columns used were `rna_id`, `disease`, `age_rounded`, `rin`, and `gPC1`–`gPC3`; `rna_id` matched every expression sample column. Disease, age, and RIN had no missing values in the analyzed metadata.
-- `gencode.v30.gene_meta.tsv.gz`: GENCODE v30 gene-symbol/Ensembl lookup with `genename` and `geneid`; useful for annotation, but expression files already supplied symbols.
-- `gencode.v30.annotation.gtf.gz`: GENCODE v30 genomic annotation (tabular GTF records, including gene/transcript/exon features); not needed for module construction.
-- `Mathys_single_nucleus.RData`: supplied single-nucleus marker object; Rscript was unavailable in this environment, and no marker matrix was used. Therefore no formal cell-type enrichment was claimed.

 # Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis of ALS Spinal Cord
 
 ## Objective
 
-The question is whether weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) can identify coordinated gene programs dysregulated in ALS spinal cord. Success means finding internally co-expressed gene modules whose eigengenes differ between ALS-spectrum and non-neurological controls, preferably with concordant signals across spinal levels and biologically interpretable hub genes. This is an observational bulk-RNA analysis: it identifies coordinated expression programs, not causal genes or cell-autonomous effects.
+Test whether WGCNA identifies coordinated gene programs dysregulated in ALS spinal cord. Success requires modules discovered from ALS samples using a weighted signed network, TOM-based module detection, module eigengenes, and quantitative ALS-versus-control testing. Cross-level replication is accepted only when a fixed gene set is transferred and its overlap and association are reported. This is an observational bulk analysis, not a causal or cell-autonomous test.
 
 ## Data Sources
 
-All paths below are relative to the working directory and were read without changing `data/`.

-- `Cervical_Spinal_Cord_gene_counts.tsv.gz`: 57,317 genes x 176 columns (2 identifiers plus 174 RNA samples). Identifiers are `ensembl_id`, `gene_name`; sample columns include `sample_124`. Raw integer counts were used for inspection only.
-- `Lumbar_Spinal_Cord_gene_counts.tsv.gz`: 57,317 x 156 (154 samples plus identifiers), same layout.
-- `Thoracic_Spinal_Cord_gene_counts.tsv.gz`: 57,317 x 54 (52 samples plus identifiers), same layout.

+def design(meta):
+    c = pd.DataFrame({'age':pd.to_numeric(meta.age_rounded,errors='coerce'),

+def signed_adj(c,p): return ((1+np.clip(c,-1,1))/2)**p
+def sf_fit(a):
+    k=a.sum(0)-1; x=np.log10(k[k>0])
+    y=np.log10(np.maximum(1,np.array([(k>=v).sum() for v in k[k>0]])))
+    return np.corrcoef(x,y)[0,1]**2 if len(x)>3 else 0
+def pc_eig(mat):
+    mat=np.asarray(mat); z=PCA(n_components=1).fit_transform(mat)[:,0]
+    return z if np.corrcoef(z,mat.mean(1))[0,1]>=0 else -z
+def network(R):
+    cor=np.corrcoef(R,rowvar=False); np.fill_diagonal(cor,0)
+    fits=[(p,sf_fit(signed_adj(cor,p))) for p in range(1,13)]
+    power=next((p for p,r in fits if r>=.80),max(fits,key=lambda z:z[1])[0])
+    A=signed_adj(cor,power); np.fill_diagonal(A,0); k=A.sum(1)
+    tom=(A@A+A)/(np.minimum.outer(k,k)+1-A+1e-9); np.fill_diagonal(tom,1)
+    Z=linkage(squareform(1-tom,checks=False),method='average')
+    lab=fcluster(Z,.60,criterion='distance'); n=pd.Series(lab).value_counts()
+    return np.array([x if n[x]>=20 else 0 for x in lab]),power,fits,tom

+
+The experiment image does not contain Bioconductor `limma` or `edgeR` (only base R packages are installed), and network/package installation is unavailable. Therefore the numeric tables above are explicitly a **Python approximation**, not results from genuine `limma::voom`, `lmFit`, or `eBayes`: they use the same complete-case cohort and covariates, a Python TMM implementation, LOWESS voom-like weights, and WLS, but do not claim empirical-Bayes moderation.
+
+The exact R code below is the reproducible requested workflow for a Bioconductor-enabled environment. It applies TPM >1 in at least 50% filtering, quantile normalization, count-scale TMM normalization, and genuine `voom`/`lmFit`/`eBayes`.
+
+```r
+library(edgeR); library(limma)
+level <- "Cervical" # repeat for Lumbar and Thoracic
+m <- read.delim(gzfile(paste0("data/",level,"_Spinal_Cord_metadata.tsv.gz")))
+m <- subset(m, disease %in% c("ALS","ALS-AD","ALS-FTD"))
+cov <- c("sex","rin","pct_mrna_bases","library_prep","site_id",paste0("gPC",1:5))
+ok <- !is.na(m$disease_duration) & complete.cases(m[,cov]); m <- m[ok,]
+samples <- m$rna_id
+cnt <- read.delim(gzfile(paste0("data/",level,"_Spinal_Cord_gene_counts.tsv.gz")), check.names=FALSE)
+tpm <- read.delim(gzfile(paste0("data/",level,"_Spinal_Cord_gene_tpm.tsv.gz")), check.names=FALSE)
+rownames(cnt) <- make.unique(cnt$ensembl_id); rownames(tpm) <- make.unique(tpm$ensembl_id)
+cnt <- as.matrix(cnt[,samples]); tpm <- as.matrix(tpm[,samples])
+keep <- rowMeans(tpm > 1) >= .50; cnt <- cnt[keep,]; tpm <- tpm[keep,]
+qn <- normalizeBetweenArrays(log2(tpm + .5), method="quantile")
+y <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(counts=cnt), method="TMM")
+m$sex <- factor(m$sex); m$library_prep <- factor(m$library_prep); m$site_id <- factor(m$site_id)
+design <- model.matrix(~ disease_duration + rin + I(rin^2) + pct_mrna_bases + sex + library_prep + site_id + gPC1+gPC2+gPC3+gPC4+gPC5, data=m)
+v <- voom(y, design, plot=FALSE)
+fit <- eBayes(lmFit(v, design), robust=TRUE)
+tab <- topTable(fit, coef="disease_duration", number=Inf, sort.by="none")
+tab$gene <- tpm[rownames(tab),"gene_name"]; tab$n <- nrow(m)
+write.table(tab, paste0(tolower(level),"_limma_ebayes.tsv"), sep="\t", quote=FALSE)
+```
+

The CHIT1 direction and TPM Spearman checks remain supported: cervical -0.5131, lumbar -0.4448, thoracic -0.4871.
